2Hollis: Audio Feature Analysis

Author

Issei Crowley

Who is 2Hollis

2Hollis was born on the 5th of janurary, 2004. His real name is Hollus Parker Frazier-Herndon. His professional music carrer has only really started recently with his first full album in August of 2022, called White Tiger. He has released 3 other albums since then, one every year, with his latest releasing on April of 2025. He currently has 4.1 million monthly listeners on spotify.

Fun fact!!!

His father is also a musician, John Herndon (also known as A Grape Dope) and he was/is the drummer of the band Tortoise

His mother is Kathryn Frazier, a prominent music industry figure who founded the PR firm Biz 3 and co-founded the record label Owsla.


There is a video of him in a car where his song jeans is playing on the radio and he is trying to open a water bottle but is very clearly struggling to open the bottle.

Data Analysis

Import data:

#these are the packages I used  for the analysis
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
#importing data from the 3 latest albums into tables
Boy<-read.csv(("boy.csv"))
Star<-read.csv(("star.csv"))
Two<-read.csv(("2.csv"))

Data preparation:

#condensing the separate albums into 1 data source
Hollis<-rbind(Boy, Star, Two)
#this is just another way of condensing the 3 albums to a single source while keeping them separated by album
df_all <- bind_rows(
  Boy  %>% mutate(Album = "Boy"),
  Star %>% mutate(Album = "Star"),
  Two  %>% mutate(Album = "Two")
)

Data frame:

This is just a sample of a few random songs from all the albums combined

df_all|>dplyr::slice_sample(n=6) |>knitr::kable(digits = 2)
Song Acousticness Danceability Energy Instrumentalness Liveness Loudness Speechiness Tempo Valence Album
FORFEIT 0.17 0.64 0.81 0.00 0.62 -3.63 0.11 135.04 0.55 Two
cope 0.07 0.50 0.63 0.01 0.28 -6.81 0.09 145.32 0.17 Star
nothing2 lose 0.10 0.70 0.64 0.00 0.60 -7.30 0.34 129.98 0.62 Two
tell me 0.01 0.63 0.56 0.00 0.12 -4.55 0.06 139.00 0.15 Star
crush 0.27 0.72 0.56 0.00 0.24 -6.70 0.18 151.01 0.56 Boy
flash 0.03 0.54 0.77 0.00 0.56 -3.90 0.12 136.08 0.27 Star

Loudness vs Energy:

df_all |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Loudness, y = Energy)) +
  geom_point(data = Boy, color = "purple", alpha = 1.0) +
  geom_point(data = Star, color = "darkgreen", alpha = 1.0) +
  geom_point(data = Two, color = "orange", alpha = 1.0) +
  geom_text(
  data = Hollis |> filter (Song %in% c("flash", "poster boy", "crush")),
  aes(label = Song),vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.7, size = 3
  )+
   labs(
    title = "Loudness vs Energy of the albums Boy, Star and Two",
    x = "Loudness",
    y = "Energy") +
      theme_minimal()

Tempo vs Danceability:

 Hollis |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Tempo, y = Danceability)) +
  geom_point(data = Boy, color = "purple", alpha = 1.0) +
  geom_point(data = Star, color = "darkgreen", alpha = 1.0) +
  geom_point(data = Two, color = "orange", alpha = 1.0) +
  geom_text(
  data = Hollis |> filter (Song %in% c("flash", "poster boy", "crush")),
      aes (label = Song),
      vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.7)+
 labs(
    title = "Tempo vs Danceability of the albums Boy, Star and Two",
    x = "Tempo",
    y = "Danceability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Acousticness between the 3 albums:

 Boy|>
   ggplot(aes(x = Acousticness)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), fill = "purple") +
  geom_density(fill = "#FF5", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Histogram of Acousticness of songs from the Album Boy",
    x = "Acousticness",
    y = "Density"
  )
 Star|>
   ggplot(aes(x = Acousticness)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), fill = "darkgreen") +
  geom_density(fill = "#FF5", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Histogram of Acousticness of songs from the Album Star",
    x = "Acousticness",
    y = "Density"
  )
 Two|>
   ggplot(aes(x = Acousticness)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), fill = "orange") +
  geom_density(fill = "#FF5", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Histogram of Acousticness of songs from the Album Two",
    x = "Acousticness",
    y = "Density"
  )

Tempo between the 3 albums

ggplot(df_all, aes(x = Album, y = Tempo)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", colour = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Boxplot of tempo by Album",
    x = "Album",
    y = "Tempo (BPM)"
  )

Valence vs Energy of the 3 abums:

Hollis |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Valence, y = Energy)) +
  geom_point(data = Boy, color = "purple", alpha = 1.0) +
  geom_point(data = Star, color = "darkgreen", alpha = 1.0) +
  geom_point(data = Two, color = "orange", alpha = 1.0) +
  geom_text(
  data = Hollis |> filter (Song %in% c("flash", "poster boy", "crush")),
      aes (label = Song),
      vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.7
)

Top 3 lowest energy songs:

Song Album Energy
promise Boy 0.03
say it Boy 0.18
eldest child Star 0.25

Conclusion:

His growth as an artist is very quick, he went from a small artist to having his own tours within 2 years of releasing his first album. Most of his music is relatively high energy, tempo and are often have a relatively high danceability score.
